summary: Mille Fiori is a quiet, cerebral drafting game where you pick a card, pass the rest, and place a token in one of five interconnected production areas, chasing multipliers from adjacency and majority bonuses. It rewards efficient, multi-track engine-building more than direct confrontation, with tension coming from anticipating what others will take from the shrinking hand.
praised: Elegant, tightly interlocking scoring systems typical of Knizia
Meaningful decisions every turn despite simple rules
Good length for the depth offered
Strong replayability from the many scoring interactions
criticised: Can feel dry or overly abstract/mathematical
Limited player interaction beyond drafting and majority contests
Analysis paralysis from optimizing across five scoring areas

interaction.kind: card drafting with majority/area contests, mostly parallel engine-building

scoring.why: Points accumulate across five distinct production areas (workshops, houses, guilds, trade, harbor), and the winner is whoever best balances and multiplies scoring across them
